title: Access Evidence Playbook - Auditor Prep
content:
Executive summary:

Purpose: This playbook is designed to help the security team and on-call engineers prepare consistent, traceable evidence for external auditors (SOC 2 / ISO 27001) around access controls, RBAC v2 changes, audit log schema and exports to SIEM, and evidence automation pipelines. It focuses on what evidence exists, where to get it, common gaps, how to remediate quickly, and a bank of prepared auditor Q&A responses and example queries.

Scope:
- Systems in-scope: Control plane (console/API), Dedicated provisioning, Private deployments control-plane telemetry where logs are centrally collected.
- Evidence types: RBAC policy artifacts, role assignment change events, authentication/authorization audit logs, KV-cache access traces where applicable, SIEM export snapshots, evidence automation runbooks and reconciliations.
- Controls targeted: SOC 2 (CC6.1, CC6.3, CC7.* access and logging related criteria) and ISO 27001 Annex A.9 (Access control), A.12 (operations) evidence mapping.

Control-to-evidence mapping (high level):
- Access control policy and role definitions (ISO A.9.1 / SOC2 access) -> source: Git repo: infra/iam/roles/*.yaml (RBAC v2 role manifests), console role catalog export (CSV), snapshot stored in evidence-bucket/iam/role-catalog-YYYYMMDD.json.
- Role assignment changes (who granted or revoked roles) -> source: auth-service audit logs (auth-grants table), GraphQL change events in audit_log.v1 (fields: event_id, principal, target, role, action, request_id, user_agent, ip, timestamp).
- Privilege escalation / admin session events -> source: elevated-session events (session_start/assume_role) recorded in centralized audit-log topic and forwarded to SIEM export in ndjson.
- Authentication events and MFA enforcement -> source: auth-service login events (success/fail), mfa_service.events, GA logs for console.
- Configuration drift for RBAC manifests -> source: periodic reconcile job reports (reconcile-run-id, diff summary, committer) and Git commit history.
- Log retention and integrity -> source: SIEM export index metadata (start_ts,end_ts,file_hash), S3 object versions and lifecycle policy docs.

Audit log schema summary (for auditors):
- Primary fields collected per event: event_id, event_type, timestamp_utc, principal_id, principal_type, target_type, target_id, action, request_id, source_ip, user_agent, context (freeform string), outcome (success|failure), svc_version, pipeline_version, ingestion_id, raw_payload_hash.
- Retention and immutability: Logs written to write-once S3 prefix with object-lock for 90 days (longer for regulated customers), all exports into SIEM are checksummed and recorded in the export manifest.
- Chain of custody: ingestion_id maps to evidence automation run metadata (job_id, collector_version, collector_checksum) in evidence_automation.jobs table.

Common gaps identified (latest review):
1) Role assignment snapshots not captured with consistent naming or timestamps (medium)
   - Impact: Harder to show historical role catalog at a specific audit date.
   - Temporary mitigation: Use Git commit history + reconcile job reports to reconstruct.
   - Remediation: Add daily artifact exporter that writes role-catalog-YYYYMMDD.json to evidence-bucket and records manifest in evidence_automation.jobs. Target due: 2026-03-15.
2) Missing request_id in a subset (~3%) of older audit events (low)
   - Impact: Difficult to correlate some API events to higher-level user actions.
   - Mitigation: Where request_id is null, correlate via timestamp+principal+ip.
   - Remediation: Enforce request_id generation at edge proxy, add validation in ingestion. Target due: 2026-02-28 (in-flight).
3) SIEM export snapshot lacks clear export manifest describing included indices (high)
   - Impact: Auditors ask for reproducible exports; without manifest we cannot prove completeness.
   - Mitigation: Produce export-level manifest retroactively for requested windows (manual).
   - Remediation: Update export pipeline to produce manifest (export_id, start_ts, end_ts, index_list, file_hash) and write to evidence-bucket. Target due: 2026-03-05.
4) Limited evidence for private deployments (customer-managed logs) (medium-high)
   - Impact: For Private customers the control evidence depends on customer environment.
   - Mitigation: Ship a lightweight evidence collector with optional attestable handshake and manifest; document recommended config in support playbook.
   - Remediation: Partner with solutions engineering to standardize onboarding checklist. Target due: 2026-04-01.

Evidence automation runbook (short):
- Who: Security SRE on-call + Evidence automation owner (Marisol Reyes).
- When: Responding to auditor artifact request or support ticket referencing a timeframe.
- Steps: 1) Confirm scope and timeframe requested, 2) Identify required artifacts from mapping above, 3) Run evidence_automation/collect_evidence.sh --start <ts> --end <ts> --type role-catalog,logs,export-manifest, 4) Validate checksums in manifest, 5) Upload a signed ZIP to secure-audit-share with index manifest and chain-of-custody email, 6) Notify auditor with index reference and short explanation of extraction method.
- Escalation: If manifest shows gaps escalate to Security Director (Evan Li) and open JIRA-SC-421.

Prepared auditor Q&A (sample questions with suggested answers and artifacts):
Q1. How do you control and record role changes for RBAC v2?
A1. Answer summary: Role definitions are stored as versioned YAML manifests in Git (repo: infra/iam). Role assignment events are emitted by the auth-service and include role, principal, request_id, committer identity and timestamp; these are persisted in the centralized audit_log.v1. Evidence artifacts: a) role-catalog-YYYYMMDD.json (snapshot exported to evidence-bucket), b) git commit log for infra/iam for the period, c) extracted audit_log.v1 events for the role assignment window (CSV).
Q2. Can you show exports sent to the SIEM for the audit window and how you verify integrity?
A2. Answer summary: We generate SIEM export batches nightly with an export manifest that lists included indices and file_hash values. The export pipeline writes both the compressed NDJSON files and a signed manifest to evidence-bucket/siem/exports/export-<id>/. Evidence artifacts: a) export manifest (export-<id>-manifest.json), b) signed NDJSON export files with checksums, c) ingestion job metadata linking ingestion_id to export_id. If the export ID is not available retroactively, we produce a manual manifest and record the reproduction steps.
Q3. How are audit logs protected from tampering and what is your retention policy?
A3. Answer summary: Raw logs are written to S3 with object-lock enabled for the configured retention period (default 90 days). All objects are versioned and checksummed; export manifests include file_hash and signer metadata. Retention policy is documented in policies/log-retention.md. Evidence artifacts: S3 object metadata printout, lifecycle policy doc, sample object metadata with version id.
Q4. We see missing request_id on a few events, how do you ensure correlation?
A4. Answer summary: Missing request_id is limited to legacy events prior to the proxy change on 2025-11-01. For those events we correlate using principal_id + timestamp +/- 2s + ip + user_agent. Our remediation plan included enforced request_id injection at the edge; rollout is complete to 95% of traffic with a follow-up ingestion-time validation task in progress. Evidence artifacts: logs showing request_id counts pre/post rollout, validation job logs.

Suggested on-the-fly auditor deliverables (quick list for immediate requests):
- Role catalog snapshot for requested date (role-catalog-YYYYMMDD.json)
- Filtered audit_log.v1 extract (CSV) with request_id, principal, action, target, timestamp
- SIEM export manifest and example NDJSON file for the requested window
- Evidence automation job record (job_id, collector_version, output_manifest) and signed ZIP of artifacts
- Short narrative (1 page) describing methods used to collect artifacts and any reconstruction steps taken

Sample queries / commands (operational examples inspectors can run or security can run and paste results):
- Get role changes between dates (psql): SELECT event_id, principal_id, action, role, timestamp_utc FROM audit_log.v1 WHERE event_type='role_change' AND timestamp_utc BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-01-31' ORDER BY timestamp_utc;
- Produce export manifest (internal tool): ./tools/siem_export --start 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z --end 2026-02-01T23:59:59Z --dry-run --manifest > export-20260201-manifest.json
- Verify checksum (bash): sha256sum export-20260201-part1.ndjson.gz > hash.txt; compare to manifest.

Appendix: Roles and responsibilities quick reference:
- Evidence automation owner: Marisol Reyes (runs and maintains collection tooling)
- Audit lead / liaison: Julian Park (primary contact for auditors)
- Security Director: Evan Li (escalation for high-severity disputes)
- SRE runbook owner: Aisha Kapoor (executes artifact extraction and validation)

Next steps (action items with owners):
- Implement daily role-catalog exporter (Marisol) - due 2026-03-15
- Complete SIEM export manifest generation pipeline (SRE infra) - due 2026-03-05
- Finish request_id enforcement validation (edge infra) - due 2026-02-28 (in progress)
- Create Private deployment evidence checklist and onboarding template (solutions eng) - due 2026-04-01

Notes and rationale: Keep this document as the canonical "auditor prep" starting point. When responding to formal auditor requests, attach the evidence manifest and a one-paragraph method note explaining how artifacts were collected and any reconstruction performed. For items with ongoing remediation, mark them transparently with issue trackers and timelines.

Document history:
- 2025-11-18 initial draft by Aisha Kapoor
- 2025-12-10 added sample queries and SIEM manifest template (Julian Park)
- 2026-02-25 remediation targets updated and export manifest added (Marisol Reyes)

End of document.
